stem: In a frequency polygon, the midpoints of the classes [10-20], [20-30], [30-40], [40-50] are plotted with frequencies 5, 10, 8, 7 respectively. The polygon is closed by adding two auxiliary classes of zero frequency on either side. What are the x-coordinates of the two auxiliary points used to close the polygon?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Class width = 10. The imaginary class before [10-20] is [0-10] with midpoint 5; the imaginary class after [40-50] is [50-60] with midpoint 55. These two points at zero frequency close the polygon.
0 and 50 are the lower boundary of the first real class and the upper boundary of the last real class, not midpoints of imaginary closing classes.
10 and 40 are the midpoints of the first and last real classes already plotted, not the auxiliary closing points.
0 and 60 are the lower boundary of [0-10] and the upper boundary of [50-60]; midpoints of those classes are 5 and 55, not 0 and 60.

explanation: A frequency polygon is closed by adding imaginary classes of zero frequency at each end. The class before [10-20] is [0-10] with midpoint (0+10)/2 = 5; the class after [40-50] is [50-60] with midpoint (50+60)/2 = 55.

explanation_sections.punchline: Closing points are midpoints of the imaginary adjacent classes: [0-10] midpoint 5 and [50-60] midpoint 55.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the model: frequency polygon is closed by extending one class width on each side at zero frequency. Class width = 10. Before first class [10-20]: imaginary class [0-10], midpoint = 5. After last class [40-50]: imaginary class [50-60], midpoint = 55.
explanation_sections.lesson: Closing points are midpoints of the adjoined phantom classes, not class boundaries.
explanation_sections.timing: 80 s. Class width = 10; first midpoint - 10 = 15 - 10 = 5; last midpoint + 10 = 45 + 10 = 55.
